question.text: Blocks m (5 kg) and M (10 kg) rest on the ground and are joined to each other by a cord that runs over a light pulley labelled B. A second cord runs from the axle of pulley B down to the ground, looping over a separate light pulley labelled A on its way. An upward pull F acts on the axle of pulley A, and both pulleys are taken to have zero mass. Taking g = 10 m/s², determine the accelerations of blocks m and M for each of the following pulls.

parts.label: a
parts.asks: Find the acceleration of m and M when F = 100 N.

parts.label: b
parts.asks: Find the acceleration of m and M when F = 300 N.

parts.label: c
parts.asks: Find the acceleration of m and M when F = 500 N.

conditions: blocks m and M start resting on the ground
m and M are joined by a cord passing over pulley B
a separate cord joins pulley B's axle to the ground, passing over pulley A
F pulls upward on pulley A's axle

figure.description: Pulley A is held up only by the upward applied force F on its own axle (nothing above it holds it up). A cord passes over pulley A: one end is tied to the ground, the other end is tied to the axle of pulley B, which hangs below A. A separate cord passes over pulley B; its two ends go straight down to block m on the left and block M on the right, both resting on the ground. Both pulleys are frictionless and massless.

solution.approach: Both pulleys are massless, so each has zero net force; this fixes the m–M string's tension at F/4, and a block moves only if that exceeds its weight.

steps.text: The string over pulley A has one end tied to the floor and the other to pulley B's axle, so its tension T₁ is the same throughout. Pulley A is massless, so the upward force F balances the two downward pulls of this string.
Pulley B is massless too, held up by T₁ and pulled down by the two strands of the string that carries m and M, so the same balance applies to it.
steps.equation: T₁ = T₂ + T₂ = 2T₂  →  T₂ = T₁/2 = F/4
steps.why_this_step: Because both pulleys are massless, this tension T₂ holds at every instant no matter how the pulleys themselves move, so it can be found without tracking their motion.

steps.text: A block leaves the floor only once T₂ exceeds its own weight; compare T₂ to m g = 50 N and M g = 100 N for each value of F.
For F = 100 N, T₂ = 25 N is less than both 50 N and 100 N, so neither block lifts off and both accelerations are zero.
For F = 300 N, T₂ = 75 N exceeds m's weight (50 N) but not M's weight (100 N), so only m lifts off; apply Newton's second law to m alone.
steps.equation: T₂ − mg = m a_m  →  75 − 50 = 5 a_m  →  a_m = 5 m/s² (up), a_M = 0

steps.text: For F = 500 N, T₂ = 125 N exceeds both weights, so both blocks lift off; apply Newton's second law to each.

final_answer.value: (a) F=100 N: a_m = 0, a_M = 0 (both remain on the floor). (b) F=300 N: a_m = 5 m/s² upward, a_M = 0 (M remains on the floor). (c) F=500 N: a_m = 15 m/s² upward, a_M = 2.5 m/s² upward

common_mistakes.text: Taking the string tension on m and M as equal to F itself instead of F/4, by forgetting that each massless pulley halves the tension passed to the next string.
For F = 100 N, wrongly assuming a block must accelerate only because F is large, without checking that the actual tension T₂ = 25 N is below both weights.
